raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

Budget Qwen video encoding by its token count before pruning, while keeping encoder-cache accounting based on retained embeddings. Fixes #63187.

## Claims

- Pruned videos can no longer overfill a step's encoder compute budget by charging only their retained embeddings.
- Duplicate inputs reuse the encoder cache, and priority preemption refunds the original compute cost. Inputs without pruning retain the existing accounting.

## Validation

RTX 4090 24 GiB, Qwen3-VL-2B-Instruct, BF16, MRV2, eager execution, TP=1. Eight distinct synthetic videos, each 16 frames at 256×256; pruning rate 0.75; encoder budget 2,048 output tokens.

| Check | Base `83c078d955cd` | Patched |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Tokens handled per visual-encoder call | `[4096]` | `[2048, 2048]` |
| New real-model regression, pruning 0.75 | Fails: `AssertionError: ([4096], 2048)` | Passes |
| Real-model regression, pruning 0.0 / 0.75 | — | 2 passed |
| Encoder cache, placeholder ranges, new scheduler cases | — | 35 passed |
| Qwen2.5/Qwen3 processors and prompt processing | — | 67 passed |
| Existing scheduler/cache/preemption regressions | — | 14 passed |
| Generation comparison against base | — | All 8 pass `check_logprobs_close`, top-5 |
| Multiprocess encoder-budget reproducer | — | Passes; calls `[512, 2048, 1536]` |

Six of eight generated token sequences are exactly equal; two differ and pass the repository's logprob comparison at their first divergence. Batch invariance was disabled. This is a serving regression check on synthetic inputs, not a video-accuracy benchmark or a throughput claim. The reproducer completes generation on both versions; it demonstrates over-budget scheduling rather than an actual OOM at this small shape.

Commands, from the repository root in the prepared environment:

```bash
# Run the new generation test on the base with only the test added, then on the fix.
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/models/multimodal/generation/test_qwen3_vl.py -k 0.75
# Before: 1 failed; AssertionError: ([4096], 2048)
# After: passes. Both pruning parameters: 2 passed.
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/models/multimodal/generation/test_qwen3_vl.py
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/v1/core/test_encoder_cache_manager.py tests/multimodal/test_inputs.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py::test_pruned_encoder_budget_with_duplicate_inputs \
  tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py::test_preemption_restores_unpruned_encoder_budget
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \
  tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_qwen3_vl.py::test_video_pruning_preserves_encoder_compute_cost \
  tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_qwen2_vl.py::test_qwen2_5_video_pruning_preserves_encoder_compute_cost \
  tests/multimodal/test_processing.py \
  -k 'preserves_encoder_compute_cost or token_matches or find_update_tokens or find_mm_placeholders or apply_prompt_updates'
```

All applicable pre-commit hooks pass, including mypy and Buildkite test tethering. The generation test is selected by the Qwen3/Gemma CI step; processor tests and CPU scheduler tests are selected by their existing steps. Upstream CI has not run.

Environment provenance: Python source from `83c078d955cd6e0c63d3b12abe669c8de936a370`, with this Python-only patch; reused CUDA extensions from the existing `db3b0f0fa` environment, not a fresh CUDA build at the base commit. Python 3.12.14, PyTorch 2.14.0+cu130, Transformers 5.20.2. Model revision `89644892e4d85e24eaac8bacfd4f463576704203`; the reused checkpoint was hash-verified. Qwen2.5 validation here covers preprocessing, not generation with Qwen2.5 weights.

## Details

Pruning happens after the vision encoder. Placeholder rewriting previously discarded the original size, so both compute admission and cache allocation used the reduced embedding count. The patch carries an optional `num_encoder_tokens` through prompt updates and placeholder metadata. It uses the same merged output-token units as encoder profiling; absent metadata falls back to the retained embedding count. Cache allocation still uses retained embeddings. No scheduler model-specific branch or GPU synchronization is added.

The intended tradeoff is smaller encoder batches when pruning is enabled; pruning still reduces decoder work and cache occupancy. The user documentation explains this distinction.

Duplicate-work checks on 2026-10-23 found no open PR referencing #63187 or implementing this fix. Searches included `63187 in:body` and `encoder budget pruning`; the related Cosmos3 encoder-CUDA-graph PR #52229 handles graph capture policies, not pre-pruning scheduler accounting.

OpenAI Codex assisted with investigation, implementation, regression validation, and drafting this description.

nodes.body:
Independent CPU component check on `95c2191`: all **25 tests** in the unchanged `test_encoder_cache_manager.py` passed, including the four new compute/cache-budget cases.

Scope: I loaded the complete `multimodal/inputs.py` and `encoder_cache_manager.py` from this head over an installed vLLM 0.32.0 / Torch 2.13.0 environment (Python 3.12, pytest 8.4.2), then ran the exact test file. This was an isolated source-overlay check, not a full-current-checkout run; the absent root marker registration produced one `cpu_test` warning. CUDA stayed uninitialized.

This supports the component accounting behavior only—not scheduler/preemption, processor, video generation, OOM or official CI qualification. No competing PR.

I'm currently validating this on H200 with the original #63187 reproducer (Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct, bf16, 16 requests × 32-frame 1280×720 videos, `max_num_batched_tokens=16384`, `gpu_memory_utilization=0.9`), since the PR's own run notes that its small shape does not reach an actual OOM.

Setup: base `83c078d955cd` vs this head `95c21910b`, at pruning rate 0.75 and 0 (control), logging patches and peak memory per vision-encoder call. I'll post the numbers here as soon as they finish.

**H200 validation of `95c21910b` against its base `83c078d955cd`** (follow-up to my note above).

Setup: 1× H200 NVL (141 GB), Qwen/Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct, bf16, the #63187 reproducer config: 16 requests × synthetic 32-frame 1280×720 videos, `max_num_batched_tokens=16384`, `gpu_memory_utilization=0.9`, in-process engine, with a hook on `Qwen3_VisionTransformer.forward` logging videos, patches, and `torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated()` per call. Prompt `<|im_start|>user\n<|video_pad|>…` (same as the PR's test). The profile run measured 1 video / 49,152 patches in every arm.

| Arm | ViT calls during generate | Max patches per call | Peak allocated | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| base, pruning 0.75 | 3 × 5 videos, 1 × 1 video | **230,400 (4.69× profile)** | **130.6 GiB** | completes, 16/16 outputs |
| PR, pruning 0.75 | 16 × 1 video | 46,080 (0.94×) | 125.67 GiB | completes, 16/16 outputs |
| base, pruning 0 | 16 × 1 video | 46,080 (0.94×) | 125.44 GiB | completes |
| PR, pruning 0 | 16 × 1 video | 46,080 (0.94×) | 125.44 GiB | completes |

- The base arm reproduces #63187's numbers exactly (230,400 patches, 4.69×, 5 videos per call). On H200 it does not OOM, but its peak (130.6 GiB) exceeds the 0.9 budget (~126.4 GiB), so smaller GPUs would OOM as reported. With the PR, every pruned call stays within the profile, and peak memory matches the unpruned control.
- Outputs: with pruning 0, the generated token IDs are identical between base and PR for 16/16 requests. With pruning 0.75, 13/16 are identical; the other 3 differ, plausibly because the vision encoder now processes 1 video per call instead of 5 (I have not checked this further). The inputs are random-noise videos, so this is a scheduling and memory check, not an accuracy benchmark.
- Separate from this PR: with the #63187 reproducer's original prompt (`<|vision_start|><|video_pad|><|vision_end|>`), both base and PR crash at pruning 0.75 in `recompute_mrope_positions` (`evs.py:337`, "expanded size of the tensor (0) must match the existing size (3014)"), i.e. #62937, fixed separately by #62959.

Setup and analysis were done with AI assistance (Claude Code); I reviewed the results.

This pull request has merge conflicts that must be resolved before it can be
merged. Please rebase the PR, @zupengwang.

https://docs.github.com/en/pull-requests/collaborating-with-pull-requests/working-with-forks/syncing-a-fork

Thanks for the detailed review, @vadiklyutiy! I previously validated this PR on H200 and would be happy to help with the follow-up fixes and regression tests.

@zupengwang, are you already working on the two cases raised above? If it'd be useful, I can take either the oversized-item scheduling case or the `recompute_mrope_positions` chunk-boundary case. Happy to coordinate so we don't duplicate work.

Follow-up to my note above: I put together a proposed follow-up fix on top of this PR's head (`95c2191`) for the two regressions @vadiklyutiy reported:

**Patch:** [b01962ba in my fork](https://github.com/MarinaMackay/vllm/commit/b01962baac4d70c1fe5669c3f0d3420155f8fb9f)

- **Oversized encoder items:** cap the scheduling charge at the full per-step encoder budget, account for that consistently in `can_allocate`, and refund the same capped amount on preemption. This allows an oversized item to run alone rather than stall.
- **mRoPE chunk boundary:** handle a chunk that starts immediately after `VISION_START`, before any media tokens have been computed.
- Added CPU regression coverage for oversized scheduling, capped-budget preemption, and the mRoPE media-placeholder boundary.

**Validation reported for this commit:**
- Targeted CPU regressions: **5 passed**.
- Qwen3-VL encoder-budget generation test on **1× H100 NVL**: **2 passed**.
- Qwen2.5-VL on **1× H100 NVL**, BF16, pruning rate 0.75, encoder budget 16,384:
  - A 34-frame 1280×720 video completed with a single 20,332-token encoder call (previously stalled).
  - Two distinct concurrent 16-frame videos both completed, with 9,568 tokens per encoder call and no mRoPE `IndexError` (previously crashed).

The two Qwen2.5-VL end-to-end scenarios were run with a temporary harness **not included in the commit**; the CPU regression tests are included. This commit is based directly on `95c2191`, so it should be straightforward to cherry-pick.

@zupengwang, feel free to incorporate this into #63291 if helpful. Happy to adjust the patch or tests based on your feedback, and I haven't opened a competing PR to avoid duplicating work.

Thanks for working on this — charging the encoder compute budget with the unpruned count is the right unit, and the budget part does what the issue asks: on the issue's Qwen3-VL recipe every vision-tower call stays within the profiled budget (max 0.938x of the profile, one video per call).

I ran the PR's diff on top of 5d35ce3934a7 and found two inputs that worked before the change and break with it, both on Qwen2.5-VL with `--video-pruning-rate`:

**1. An item whose unpruned count exceeds the whole compute budget is never scheduled.**
The charge is the full unpruned count with no cap, and `can_allocate` now refuses any item above the budget. The input processor still validates only the pruned count, so the request is accepted and then waits forever. Example: one 34-frame 720p video, 20,332 unpruned embeddings against a budget of 16,384. On the base commit it is answered; with this PR the request stays at the placeholder offset (`num_computed_tokens=15`) with no encoder call at all. This hits any long Qwen2.5-VL video, since that processor caps pixels per frame rather than per video, and a Qwen3-VL request with a large per-request `size` too. Charging `min(num_unpruned, encoder_compute_budget)` lets such an item run alone in its step, which is what happened before.

**2. Two concurrent pruned videos now crash in `recompute_mrope_positions`.**
With the higher charge the second video no longer fits in the same step, so its chunk starts right at the placeholder. `recompute_mrope_positions` in `vllm/multimodal/evs.py` does not expect a chunk to start there for media without timestamp tokens and raises `IndexError: index 0 is out of bounds` (line 297 on that commit). Example: two distinct 16-frame videos sent at once. This works on the base commit. The fix is to accept a chunk that starts right after the vision-start token of the chunk's first media.

Separately, the issue's recipe still ends with `RuntimeError: The expanded size of the tensor (0) must match the existing size (3014)` on this PR, but that comes from vllm-project/vllm#62937 (outer `<|vision_start|>` from newer transformers), which vllm-project/vllm#62959 addresses, so it is not this PR's to fix.

On the tests: the end-to-end check that no vision-tower call exceeds the budget, the preemption-restore test and the duplicate-input test are great. I'd add two cases for the paths the new charge creates: an item larger than the budget being scheduled alone, and a chunk that starts at a media placeholder in `recompute_mrope_positions`.

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+
+import numpy as np
+import pytest
+
+from vllm import SamplingParams
+from vllm.multimodal import MULTIMODAL_REGISTRY
+from vllm.multimodal.encoder_budget import MultiModalBudget
+
+
+def _observe_encoder_tokens(model):
+    model.encoder_token_counts = []
+
+    def record(module, args):
+        model.encoder_token_counts.append(
+            args[0].shape[0] // module.spatial_merge_size**2
+        )
+
+    model.visual.register_forward_pre_hook(record)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.core_model
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("model", ["Qwen/Qwen3-VL-2B-Instruct"])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("pruning_rate", [0.0, 0.75])
+def test_video_pruning_respects_encoder_budget(
+    vllm_runner, model, pruning_rate, monkeypatch
+):
+    # Enqueue every request before scheduling to make the batch deterministic.
+    monkeypatch.setenv("VLLM_ENABLE_V1_MULTIPROCESSING", "0")
+    prompt = (
+        "<|im_start|>user\n<|video_pad|>"
+        "Describe the video in one sentence.<|im_end|>\n<|im_start|>assistant\n"
+    )
+    metadata = {
+        "fps": 2.0,
+        "duration": 8.0,
+        "total_num_frames": 16,
+        "frames_indices": list(range(16)),
+        "video_backend": "opencv",
+        "do_sample_frames": False,
+    }
+    inputs = [
+        {
+            "prompt": prompt,
+            "multi_modal_data": {
+                "video": [(np.full((16, 256, 256, 3), i * 30, np.uint8), metadata)]
+            },
+        }
+        for i in range(8)
+    ]
+    with vllm_runner(
+        model,
+        dtype="bfloat16",
+        enforce_eager=True,
+        enable_chunked_prefill=True,
+        max_model_len=4096,
+        max_num_batched_tokens=2048,
+        max_num_seqs=8,
+        gpu_memory_utilization=0.65,
+        enable_prefix_caching=False,
+        limit_mm_per_prompt={"image": 0, "video": 1},
+        video_pruning_rate=pruning_rate,
+        mm_processor_cache_gb=0,
+        mm_processor_kwargs={
+            "videos_kwargs": {
+                "size": {"shortest_edge": 65536, "longest_edge": 1048576},
+                "num_frames": 16,
+            }
+        },
+    ) as runner:
+        llm = runner.get_llm()
+        budget = MultiModalBudget(
+            llm.llm_engine.vllm_config, MULTIMODAL_REGISTRY
+        ).encoder_compute_budget
+        runner.apply_model(_observe_encoder_tokens)
+        outputs = llm.generate(inputs, SamplingParams(temperature=0, max_tokens=16))
+        counts = runner.apply_model(lambda model: model.encoder_token_counts)[0]
+
+        assert len(outputs) == len(inputs)
+        assert all(output.outputs[0].token_ids for output in outputs)
+        assert sum(counts) > budget  # The workload requires multiple encoder steps.
+        assert max(counts) <= budget, (counts, budget)

@@ -410,6 +410,36 @@ def _build_qwen2_5_vl_video_mm_data(num_frames: int, fps: float) -> dict[str, An
     return {"video": [(video, metadata)]}
 
 
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("pruning_rate", [0.0, 0.75])
+def test_qwen2_5_video_pruning_preserves_encoder_compute_cost(pruning_rate):
+    ctx = build_model_context(
+        "Qwen/Qwen2.5-VL-3B-Instruct",
+        limit_mm_per_prompt={"image": 0, "video": 1},
+        mm_processor_cache_gb=1,
+        model_config_kwargs={"video_pruning_rate": pruning_rate},
+    )
+    processor = MULTIMODAL_REGISTRY.create_processor(ctx.model_config)
+    cache = MultiModalProcessorOnlyCache(ctx.model_config)
+    mm_items = processor.info.parse_mm_data(
+        _build_qwen2_5_vl_video_mm_data(num_frames=16, fps=2.0)
+    )
+    for _ in range(2):
+        result = processor(
+            "<|vision_start|><|video_pad|><|vision_end|>",
+            mm_items=mm_items,
+            cache=cache,
+        )
+        position = result["mm_placeholders"]["video"][0]
+        grid = result["mm_kwargs"].get_data()["video_grid_thw"][0]
+        merge_size = processor.info.get_hf_config().vision_config.spatial_merge_size

Independent CPU component check on `95c2191`: all **25 tests** in the unchanged `test_encoder_cache_manager.py` passed, including the four new compute/cache-budget cases.

Scope: I loaded the complete `multimodal/inputs.py` and `encoder_cache_manager.py` from this head over an installed vLLM 0.32.0 / Torch 2.13.0 environment (Python 3.12, pytest 8.4.2), then ran the exact test file. This was an isolated source-overlay check, not a full-current-checkout run; the absent root marker registration produced one `cpu_test` warning. CUDA stayed uninitialized.

This supports the component accounting behavior only—not scheduler/preemption, processor, video generation, OOM or official CI qualification. No competing PR.

I'm currently validating this on H200 with the original #63187 reproducer (Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct, bf16, 16 requests × 32-frame 1280×720 videos, `max_num_batched_tokens=16384`, `gpu_memory_utilization=0.9`), since the PR's own run notes that its small shape does not reach an actual OOM.

Setup: base `83c078d955cd` vs this head `95c21910b`, at pruning rate 0.75 and 0 (control), logging patches and peak memory per vision-encoder call. I'll post the numbers here as soon as they finish.

Prompt `<|im_start|>user\n<|video_pad|>…` (same as the PR's test). The profile run measured 1 video / 49,152 patches in every arm.

| Arm | ViT calls during generate | Max patches per call | Peak allocated | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| base, pruning 0.75 | 3 × 5 videos, 1 × 1 video | **230,400 (4.69× profile)** | **130.6 GiB** | completes, 16/16 outputs |
| PR, pruning 0.75 | 16 × 1 video | 46,080 (0.94×) | 125.67 GiB | completes, 16/16 outputs |
| base, pruning 0 | 16 × 1 video | 46,080 (0.94×) | 125.44 GiB | completes |
| PR, pruning 0 | 16 × 1 video | 46,080 (0.94×) | 125.44 GiB | completes |

- The base arm reproduces #63187's numbers exactly (230,400 patches, 4.69×, 5 videos per call). On H200 it does not OOM, but its peak (130.6 GiB) exceeds the 0.9 budget (~126.4 GiB), so smaller GPUs would OOM as reported. With the PR, every pruned call stays within the profile, and peak memory matches the unpruned control.
- Outputs: with pruning 0, the generated token IDs are identical between base and PR for 16/16 requests. With pruning 0.75, 13/16 are identical; the other 3 differ, plausibly because the vision encoder now processes 1 video per call instead of 5 (I have not checked this further). The inputs are random-noise videos, so this is a scheduling and memory check, not an accuracy benchmark.

@zupengwang, are you already working on the two cases raised above? If it'd be useful, I can take either the oversized-item scheduling case or the `recompute_mrope_positions` chunk-boundary case. Happy to coordinate so we don't duplicate work.

Follow-up to my note above: I put together a proposed follow-up fix on top of this PR's head (`95c2191`) for the two regressions @vadiklyutiy reported:

**Patch:** [b01962ba in my fork](https://github.com/MarinaMackay/vllm/commit/b01962baac4d70c1fe5669c3f0d3420155f8fb9f)

- **Oversized encoder items:** cap the scheduling charge at the full per-step encoder budget, account for that consistently in `can_allocate`, and refund the same capped amount on preemption. This allows an oversized item to run alone rather than stall.
- **mRoPE chunk boundary:** handle a chunk that starts immediately after `VISION_START`, before any media tokens have been computed.
- Added CPU regression coverage for oversized scheduling, capped-budget preemption, and the mRoPE media-placeholder boundary.

reviews.body:
Thanks for working on this — charging the encoder compute budget with the unpruned count is the right unit, and the budget part does what the issue asks: on the issue's Qwen3-VL recipe every vision-tower call stays within the profiled budget (max 0.938x of the profile, one video per call).

I ran the PR's diff on top of 5d35ce3934a7 and found two inputs that worked before the change and break with it, both on Qwen2.5-VL with `--video-pruning-rate`:

**1. An item whose unpruned count exceeds the whole compute budget is never scheduled.**
The charge is the full unpruned count with no cap, and `can_allocate` now refuses any item above the budget. The input processor still validates only the pruned count, so the request is accepted and then waits forever. Example: one 34-frame 720p video, 20,332 unpruned embeddings against a budget of 16,384. On the base commit it is answered; with this PR the request stays at the placeholder offset (`num_computed_tokens=15`) with no encoder call at all. This hits any long Qwen2.5-VL video, since that processor caps pixels per frame rather than per video, and a Qwen3-VL request with a large per-request `size` too. Charging `min(num_unpruned, encoder_compute_budget)` lets such an item run alone in its step, which is what happened before.

**2. Two concurrent pruned videos now crash in `recompute_mrope_positions`.**
With the higher charge the second video no longer fits in the same step, so its chunk starts right at the placeholder. `recompute_mrope_positions` in `vllm/multimodal/evs.py` does not expect a chunk to start there for media without timestamp tokens and raises `IndexError: index 0 is out of bounds` (line 297 on that commit). Example: two distinct 16-frame videos sent at once. This works on the base commit. The fix is to accept a chunk that starts right after the vision-start token of the chunk's first media.

Separately, the issue's recipe still ends with `RuntimeError: The expanded size of the tensor (0) must match the existing size (3014)` on this PR, but that comes from vllm-project/vllm#62937 (outer `<|vision_start|>` from newer transformers), which vllm-project/vllm#62959 addresses, so it is not this PR's to fix.

On the tests: the end-to-end check that no vision-tower call exceeds the budget, the preemption-restore test and the duplicate-input test are great. I'd add two cases for the paths the new charge creates: an item larger than the budget being scheduled alone, and a chunk that starts at a media placeholder in `recompute_mrope_positions`.
